newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger, buoyed by U.S. rally.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger, buoyed by U.S. rally.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Tuesday, pulled up by a rally in U.S. fixed income markets, following the release of weaker-than-expected U.S. employment cost data, dealers said.

"The great wage inflation scare seems to have dissipated," said Dan Kelly, director of financial markets research with CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc. "I think we just got caught in the updraft of the U.S."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.53 to C$110.30 to yield 7.130 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 1 - 31/32 to yield 6.68 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 45 basis points from 41 basis points at Monday's close.

The U.S. Labor Department this morning reported that employment costs for the third quarter rose 0.6 percent, below expectations of a 0.8 percent rise. The report sparked a rally in U.S. Treasuries, which pulled the Canadian bond market higher. The report increased expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve would not raise interest rates for the rest of the year.
"If there's no wage inflation, there's no way the Fed's going to tighten," said CIBC Wood Gundy's Kelly.
Analysts said Canadian economic data out this morning, including the industrial product price index for September, had little market impact.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$1.22 to C$103.68 to yield 6.496 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 1 - 9/32 to yield 6.38 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to 12 basis points from 10 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.18 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.14 percent.
